en: The brain very literally, very clearly, plainly is a computer.
zh: 大脑从字面上、非常清楚、直白地说，就是一台计算机。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can solve computational problems by arranging matter in a certain way and then taking your hands off and pressing go.
zh: 你可以通过以某种方式排列物质来解决计算问题，然后把手拿开，按下“开始”。

speaker: Unknown
en: We talk about being a brain in a vat.
zh: 我们谈论做缸中之脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what the skull is.
zh: 颅骨就是那个缸。

en: The brain is connected to the environment through a small number of wires, the cranial and spinal nerves, these little cables that carry your interaction with the world.
zh: 大脑通过少量导线与环境相连，即脑神经和脊神经，这些小电缆承载着你与世界的交互。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you can get the visual signal, auditory signal, balance, motor, in and out of the brain, that is an end in itself.
zh: 如果你能让视觉信号、听觉信号、平衡觉、运动信号进出大脑，这本身就是目的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is the central object.
zh: 那才是核心对象。

speaker: Unknown
en: The retinal prosthesis right now
zh: 视网膜假体现在

speaker: Unknown
en: I think is a great proof of concept that we're on the right track.
zh: 我认为是一个很好的概念验证，证明我们走在正确的轨道上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody had previously ever been able to restore a form vision image in the mind's eye of a blind patient in this way.
zh: 以前从来没有人能够以这种方式在盲人患者的心灵之眼中恢复某种形式的视觉图像。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to add depth of grayscale.
zh: 我们需要增加灰度深度。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think we could see a path to get at least red and green.
zh: 我们认为可以看到一条实现至少红色和绿色的路径。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's ways that we can compound upon this path through an engineering process to make a product that's better and better.
zh: 因此，有很多方法可以通过工程流程在这条路径上不断叠加，做出越来越好的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome back to No Priors.

zh: 今天和我一起的是 Max Hodak,他是 Science 的创始人兼 CEO,此前曾任职于 Neuralink。

speaker: Unknown
en: We talk about Prima, the implant that helps people who have gone blind see again, which just got regulatory approval in Europe, their quest to sustain the human experience and substrate independence for the brain.
zh: 我们会聊到 Prima,这个帮助失明者重见光明的植入物，它刚刚获得了欧洲的监管批准；还会聊到他们延续人类体验和大脑基质独立性的探索。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also talk about alignable representations between AI models and the future of neuroscience.
zh: 我们还会聊到 AI 模型之间的可对齐表征，以及神经科学的未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome, Max.
zh: 欢迎，Max。

speaker: Unknown
en: Max, thanks so much for doing this.
zh: Max,非常感谢你来做这期节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for having me.
zh: 谢谢你们的邀请。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for anyone who is not familiar with science, can you just describe a little bit about why you start the company, leaving Neuralink, what the mission is?
zh: 那么对于还不熟悉 Science 的听众，你能简单介绍一下你为什么创立这家公司、离开 Neuralink,以及使命是什么吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Fundamentally, we're a medical device company.
zh: 从根本上说，我们是一家医疗设备公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think if the mission of lowercase s science is to use a differentiated understanding of the universe to improve the human condition, I mean, that's the mission of uppercase s science.
zh: 但我认为，如果小写 s 的 science(科学)的使命是利用对宇宙的差异化理解来改善人类境况，我的意思是，那就是大写 S 的 Science 的使命。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what we do.
zh: 这就是我们所做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's specifically an understanding of how to work with the brain to get big effect sizes that you don't get in medicine often.
zh: 具体来说，就是理解如何与大脑协作，以获得医学中不常见的大效应量。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our main product is a retinal prosthesis.
zh: 我们的主要产品是视网膜假体。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can think of it like a cochlear implant for the eye.
zh: 你可以把它想象成眼睛的人工耳蜗。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cochlear implants are some of the biggest impacts in all of medicine.
zh: 人工耳蜗是整个医学领域影响最大的成果之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, if you've ever seen a video of a newborn turning it on for the first time, it's striking.
zh: 我的意思是，如果你看过新生儿第一次开机时的视频，那是非常震撼的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And our goal is to build things like that, including our primal retinal prosthesis.
zh: 我们的目标就是打造这样的产品，包括我们的 prima 视网膜假体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for people who are not familiar with that, it's a chip that is inserted with glasses.
zh: 对于不熟悉它的人，这是一块随眼镜一起植入的芯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a tiny chip that's implanted under the retina in the back of the eye for patients that have gone blind due to loss of the light-sensitive cells in the eye.
zh: 它是一块植入视网膜下方、位于眼球后部的微小芯片，适用于因眼球中感光细胞丧失而失明的患者。

speaker: Unknown
en: So specifically, this is diseases like macular degeneration, which our clinical trial was done, and we're about to do studies in retinitis pigmentosa and Stargardt and a couple other diseases.
zh: 具体来说，就是像黄斑变性这样的疾病，我们的临床试验就是针对它做的，我们即将开展针对视网膜色素变性、Stargardt 病和其他几种疾病的研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a chip that sits under the retina and then converts it.
zh: 它是一块位于视网膜下方的芯片，然后进行转换。

speaker: Unknown
en: The patient wears glasses that have a laser projector that projects an image onto the implant that then stimulates the retina to bypass the dead rods and cones and stimulate the retina directly to get a visual signal back into the brain.
zh: 患者佩戴的眼镜上有一个激光投影仪，将图像投影到植入物上，植入物再刺激视网膜，绕过死亡的视杆细胞和视锥细胞，直接刺激视网膜，把视觉信号重新送回大脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you go from, we should have like a nick invasively in the brain to this particular form factor as the first premise?
zh: 你是如何从“我们应该在大脑中非侵入式地放置一个 nick”走到这个特定形态作为首要前提的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So when we started the company, we had a couple ideas.
zh: 我们创立公司的时候，有几个想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the ideas was the bio-hybrid neural interface direction, where instead of placing metal wires into the brain or genetically modifying the brain, what we do is we engraft in living neurons that grow in and form new biological connections.
zh: 其中一个想法是生物混合神经接口方向，不是把金属导线放入大脑或对大脑进行基因改造，而是移植活体神经元，让它们长入并形成新的生物连接。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a big research project.
zh: 那是一个大型研究项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very exciting research, but also needed to be paired with another near-term business.
zh: 这是非常令人兴奋的研究，但也需要与另一个近期业务相配套。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we asked ourselves, like, what was the most valuable thing we could do?
zh: 我们问自己，我们能做的最有价值的事情是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And we thought that we could restore vision to the blind with the resources available to us and where the state of the field was in early 2021.
zh: 我们认为，凭借我们可获得的资源以及 2021 年初该领域的发展状况，我们可以让盲人恢复视力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you want to do that,
zh: 所以如果你想做到这一点，

speaker: Unknown
en: We have to start from this understanding of like, how does the brain get vision?
zh: 我们必须从这样一个理解出发：大脑是如何获得视觉的？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is vision in the brain?
zh: 大脑中的视觉是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And you could look at the retina, which is obviously how vision gets into the brain, the first place it's created.
zh: 你可以看视网膜，它显然是视觉进入大脑的途径，是视觉最初被创造的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first stop of the optic nerve into the brain is a structure called the lateral geniculate nucleus and the thalamus, so that you could think, oh, we'll stimulate the LGN.
zh: 视神经进入大脑的第一站是一个叫做外侧膝状体核的结构，位于丘脑中，所以你可能会想，哦，我们可以刺激 LGN。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the connection from there is visual cortex.
zh: 然后从那里连接的是视觉皮层。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's half a billion cells up at the back of the brain.
zh: 它在大脑后部有五亿个细胞。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you want to restore vision, you can think, I can go into the retina, I can go in through the thalamus, or I can go in through V1.
zh: 所以如果你想恢复视觉，你可以想，我可以进入视网膜，我可以穿过丘脑进入，或者我可以进入 V1。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a bunch of scientific, technical reasons that lead you to think if you have an optic nerve, you want to be in the retina.
zh: 有一堆科学上、技术上的理由让你认为，如果你有视神经，你就应该待在视网膜。

speaker: Unknown
en: And from there, you have a choice of do you stimulate?
zh: 从那里开始，你面临一个选择：你要不要刺激？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's two types of cells and there's a couple of different ways you could stimulate them.
zh: 有两种类型的细胞，而且有几种不同的方式可以刺激它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we explored kind of all variants of that early on.
zh: 所以我们早期探索了几乎所有这些变体。

speaker: Unknown
en: We developed an in-house gene therapy that affected the retin in one direction.
zh: 我们开发了一个内部的基因疗法，它在一个方向上影响 retina。

speaker: Unknown
en: We did a survey of electrical stimulators.
zh: 我们调研了电刺激器。

speaker: Unknown
en: We looked at ultrasound.
zh: 我们研究了超声波。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what we ended up doing is we developed indigenously a state-of-the-art gene therapy, which is probably going to humans next year, as well as we found the state-of-the-art out there in the world of people electrically stimulating the retina.
zh: 而我们最终做的是，我们自主开发了一种最先进的基因疗法，它大概明年就会进入人体试验，同时我们也找到了世界上在电刺激视网膜领域最先进的技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there was a company in France called Pixium that back in late 2022
zh: 当时在法国有一家叫 Pixium 的公司，在 2022 年底

speaker: Unknown
en: had by far the state of the artwork.
zh: 拥有迄今为止最先进的技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was originally developed by an inventor at Stanford and then licensed to this small French company, and they were in the middle of clinical trials.
zh: 它最初由斯坦福的一位发明家开发，然后授权给了这家法国小公司，当时他们正处于临床试验的中期。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we got to know them over the course of a couple of years, and then we're in a position to acquire them when we saw something that I think kind of nobody else really saw at the time.
zh: 我们在几年的过程中逐渐熟悉了他们，然后当我们看到了一件我认为当时几乎没人真正看到的东西时，我们处于能够收购他们的位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that, I mean, that deal has turned out to be great.
zh: 而那笔交易，我是说，事实证明非常成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you talk about the recent CE designation regulatory approval you got?
zh: 你能谈谈你们最近获得的 CE 认定监管批准吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so it took us about two years for post-acquisition to get it to the place where this was possible.
zh: 是的，收购之后我们花了大约两年时间才把它推进到可以实现这一步的程度。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we just, in July, got marketing approval in Europe for Prima to start commercially selling it there.
zh: 但我们刚刚在 7 月获得了欧洲的上市批准，Prima 可以开始在那里进行商业销售。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's a major milestone.
zh: 所以这是一个重大里程碑。

speaker: Unknown
en: That means it's really commercially available.
zh: 这意味着它真正可以商业化了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first sales will happen in the coming weeks.
zh: 首批销售将在接下来的几周内发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's amazing.
zh: 那太了不起了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think most people think of anything in the BCI field as, you know, a moonshot project that may or may not pan out 10 years from now.
zh: 我想大多数人认为 BCI 领域的任何事情都是，你知道，一个登月项目，十年后可能成也可能不成。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I mean, people forget that the moonshot worked.
zh: 嗯，我是说，人们忘了登月计划是成功的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we went, we left like boot prints on the moon.
zh: 就像我们，我们在月球上留下了脚印。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this comparison, I mean, I think that there's,
zh: 所以这个类比，我是说，我认为，

speaker: Unknown
en: It has gotten used in Silicon Valley to mean these things that have extremely long odds and are unlikely to work, and therefore, we can vaporize a bunch of investor money just fine.
zh: 它在硅谷已经被用来指那些胜率极低、不太可能成功的事情，因此，我们可以理所当然地烧掉一大堆投资人的钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, when we went to the moon, we did it.
zh: 但事实是，当我们去月球的时候，我们做到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Historically, the success rate of moonshots is higher than I think people give them credit for.
zh: 从历史上看，登月式项目的成功率比人们认为的要高。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the most important things is having a real business here, and this is the start of that.
zh: 其中最重要的事情之一就是在这里拥有一个真正的生意，而这正是它的开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I ask how you when you were exploring both different signaling pathways and form factors and just conditions to go attack or how you thought about scope of timeline and engineering cost and risk?
zh: 我能问一下，当你们在探索不同的信号通路和形态因子以及攻击的条件时，你们是如何考虑时间线、工程成本和风险的范围的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Were you just looking for like the like big enough to be useful and feasible in some period of time?
zh: 你们是不是只是在寻找那种，比如，足够大到有用、并且在某段时间内可行的东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or how did you think about funding the project and how long it could take?
zh: 还是如何考虑项目的资金投入以及它可能需要多长时间？

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's three elements to our pipeline.
zh: 我们的管线有三个要素。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first is our work in vision, second is our bio-hybrid neural interfaces, and the third is our work in a different area of medicine, perfusion, a program called VESSEL.
zh: 第一个是我们在视觉方面的工作，第二个是我们的生物混合神经接口，第三个是我们在另一个医学领域的工作，灌注，一个叫 VESSEL 的项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: These three things together form kind of the minimum set of things that I think if they're successful in the time scale of 10 to 15 years could
zh: 这三件事合在一起构成了我认为的最小集合，如果它们在 10 到 15 年的时间尺度上成功，可以

speaker: Unknown
en: Really drive, I think, a significant revolution in medicine broadly.
zh: 真正推动，我认为，整个医学领域的重大革命。

speaker: Unknown
en: People have spent huge amounts of time and money looking for drugs to restore vision or to restore hearing or to stop Parkinson's or to help paralyzed people move again.
zh: 人们花了大量的时间和金钱去寻找能恢复视觉或恢复听力或阻止帕金森病或帮助瘫痪者重新行动的药物。

speaker: Unknown
en: The biology and the molecular detail required to make a drug has been very difficult.
zh: 制造药物所需的生物学和分子层面的细节一直非常困难。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 说实话，人类在这方面并不那么擅长。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the other hand, the brain is a computer, and when you deal with the brain as a computer, you get these things to work.
zh: 另一方面，大脑是一台计算机，而当你把大脑当作计算机来处理时，你就能让这些东西工作起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just, again, you don't see demonstration, you don't see things in medicine like a cochlear implant being turned on or a deep brain stimulator being turned on.
zh: 只不过，再说一次，你看不到演示，你在医学中看不到像人工耳蜗被打开或者深部脑刺激器被打开这样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you can implant a quadriplegic patient in motor cortex.
zh: 我是说，你可以在一位四肢瘫痪患者的运动皮层植入电极。

speaker: Unknown
en: And have them playing video games in like an hour.
zh: 然后让他们在一小时内就开始玩视频游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just don't really see things like this in most drugs.
zh: 你在大多数药物中真的看不到这样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's this- In small molecule, random walk, sifting in nature.
zh: 所以有这种—— 在小分子里，随机游走，在自然界里筛选。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, small molecules especially are super hard.
zh: 我是说，小分子尤其难。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you can do some super highly engineered-
zh: 我是说，你可以做一些高度工程化的——

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a patient-specific CAR-T and instead you get like a giant immune overreaction.
zh: 那是患者特异性的 CAR-T，结果你却得到一场巨大的免疫过激反应。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like if I put electrodes in M1, you will probably be using a computer in an hour.
zh: 这就像如果我把电极放进 M1，你可能一小时内就在用电脑了。

en: And so it's just it's easier, it's more amenable to biology in many ways.
zh: 所以它就是更容易，在很多方面更符合生物学的规律。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 答案可能是否定的。

en: And then everybody goes home.
zh: 然后所有人就都回家了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas here, we have a clear sense of how to make the thing better.
zh: 而在这里，我们对如何把东西做得更好有清晰的认识。

speaker: Unknown
en: The retinal prosthesis right now I think is a great proof of concept that we're on the right track.
zh: 视网膜假体现在我认为是一个很好的概念验证，证明我们走在正确的轨道上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody had previously ever been able to restore a form vision image in the mind's eye of a blind patient in this way.
zh: 以前从来没有人能够以这种方式在盲人的心目中恢复一种视觉图像。

speaker: Unknown
en: But at the same time, it's a small field of view.
zh: 但与此同时，它的视野很小。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like looking through a straw.
zh: 就像透过一根吸管看东西。

en: It's only black and white.
zh: 而且只有黑白的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to add depth of grayscale.
zh: 我们需要增加灰度的深度。

speaker: Unknown
en: We see a path to get at least red and green.
zh: 我们看到了一条能实现至少红色和绿色的路径。

speaker: Unknown
en: Blue is a little bit trickier.
zh: 蓝色则稍微棘手一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's ways that we can compound upon this path through an engineering process to make a product that's better and better.
zh: 所以我们可以通过一个工程过程在这条路径上不断叠加，做出一个越来越好的产品。

en: Yeah, I mean, in the clinical trial, I mean, the main thing was just the existence proof of like that success was a possible outcome, right?
zh: 是的，我是说，在临床试验中，我的意思是，最主要的事情就是存在性证明，就像成功是一个可能的结果，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like that we had patients filling in Sudoku puzzles or crossword puzzles.

en: And so I saw some of these patients, some of these videos, met with one of the patients, talked to the surgeons.
zh: 所以我见到了一些这样的患者，看了一些这些视频，和其中一位患者会面，和外科医生交谈过。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, this is one of those things that seems too good to be true.
zh: 我的意思是，这是那种看起来好得不真实的事情之一。

en: It'll feel like it's fully formed, but until you really sit down and try to write it out, it isn't really.
zh: 它会感觉是已经完全成形的,但直到你真正坐下来试着把它写出来之前,它其实并不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that feeling is misleading.
zh: 而且我认为那种感觉是误导性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's this 10-bit per second kind of famous cognitive bottleneck.
zh: 于是就有了这个著名的每秒 10 比特的认知瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's this observation that the brain seems to process information.
zh: 有这样一个观察:大脑似乎处理信息时——

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a bunch of ways you can triangulate this.
zh: 有很多方法可以对这一点进行三角验证。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can put somebody with a perfect memory on a helicopter ride over Manhattan, ask them to draw what they saw, and then you look at all the details.
zh: 你可以让一个拥有完美记忆力的人乘直升机飞越曼哈顿上空,让他画出看到的东西,然后你去看所有的细节。

speaker: Unknown
en: It works to about 10 bits per second over a course of an hour or two.
zh: 在一到两个小时的过程中,它大致是每秒 10 比特。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a bunch of different independent lines of evidence for this.
zh: 关于这一点有一系列不同的独立证据。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's some deeply evolved cognitive bottleneck about that.
zh: 所以这里存在某种深度演化出来的认知瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that this kind of rolls up through language.
zh: 而我认为这一瓶颈通过语言一路贯穿下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: But even if you take that, it probably would be nice to be able to walk down the street with a cap on and ask questions to my AI through monologue.
zh: 但即便如此,能戴着某种头戴设备走在街上、通过内心独白向我的 AI 提问,大概也很不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: That might be possible.
zh: 那有可能是可行的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's probably some combination of EEG and MEG that might be capable of this.
zh: EEG 和 MEG 的某种组合可能有能力做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is still just like a different type of product.
zh: 但那仍然只是一种不同类型的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is not the thing we are trying.
zh: 那不是我们正在尝试的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like a brain keyboard is, it might be valuable.
zh: 像一个大脑键盘这样的东西,它可能是有价值的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It might turn out to be like AR glasses where it's just, our attention was already fully 100% occupied and putting it on the face didn't really change that.
zh: 它可能会变成类似 AR 眼镜那样的东西——我们的注意力本来就已经 100% 完全被占据了,把它放到脸上并没有真正改变这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were already consuming all of the available time.
zh: 我们本来就已经在消耗所有可用的时间了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But at the other end of that spectrum are things like
zh: 但在那个光谱的另一端,是一些像

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are the things that we are focused on, not brain keyboard.
zh: 那些才是我们专注于的事情,而不是大脑键盘。

speaker: Unknown
en: Both of these are potentially BCI problems or products, but very different types of companies that will build them, just as I think you have a huge range of drug companies.
